12185659.title: Ang_Totoong_Narcolist
12185659.extract:
# Ang Totoong Narcolist

**Ang Totoong Narcolist** (transl. The True Narcolist) is a series of viral videos released in April 2019 that accused members of the family and associates of then-Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte of involvement in the illegal drug trade. The videos featured a hooded narrator known as "Bikoy," who claimed to be a former record-keeper for a drug syndicate. The narrator was later identified as Peter Joemel Advincula.

The controversy surrounding the videos led to a complex series of legal and political events. Advincula initially sought legal aid from the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) to stand by his allegations, only to surrender to the Philippine National Police (PNP) weeks later. Upon his surrender, Advincula recanted his claims, alleging that the videos were fabricated and orchestrated by the political opposition, specifically the Liberal Party and Senator Antonio Trillanes IV, as part of a plot dubbed "Project Sodoma" to oust President Duterte .

Advincula's retraction resulted in the filing of sedition complaints against Vice President Leni Robredo and other opposition figures. In 2020, the Department of Justice (DOJ) cleared Robredo but indicted Trillanes, Advincula, and nine others for conspiracy to commit sedition . In May 2023, a Manila court convicted Advincula of perjury for making false statements regarding the alleged involvement of human rights lawyers in the plot . Subsequently, in September 2023, a Quezon City court acquitted Trillanes, Advincula, and their co-accused of the conspiracy to commit sedition charges due to insufficiency of evidence .

## Content and Allegations

The video series, titled *Ang Totoong Narcolist*, was uploaded to YouTube and shared across various social media platforms beginning April 2, 2019 . The videos were narrated by a hooded figure who identified himself as "Bikoy." He claimed to be a former member of a drug syndicate operating in Southern Luzon and the Visayas, specifically tasked with recording financial transactions .

### Specific Accusations
The videos alleged that the syndicate provided "tara" (grease money) to high-ranking individuals. Key allegations included:
* **Paolo Duterte:** The President's son was accused of receiving monthly payoffs. Bikoy claimed Paolo Duterte used the code names "POLO DELTA-TSG01" and "ALPHA TIERRA-0029" in the syndicate's records . The videos asserted that Paolo Duterte had a dragon tattoo on his back containing the alphanumeric code, which served as proof of his membership in the triad .
* **Christopher "Bong" Go:** The President's former special assistant and eventual Senator was accused of being a conduit for drug money .
* **Manases Carpio:** The husband of Davao City Mayor Sara Duterte was also implicated in the financial records presented in the videos .
* **Veronica Duterte:** The President's minor daughter was mentioned in relation to the alleged transactions, a point that drew specific condemnation from the administration .

### "Dragon Tattoo" Controversy
A focal point of the allegations was the claim regarding a dragon tattoo on Paolo Duterte's back. Opposition Senator Leila de Lima challenged Paolo Duterte to show his back to disprove the allegations . Paolo Duterte refused to show his back, citing his right to privacy and stating he would not dignify the claims of his "enemies" .

## Investigation and "Bikoy" Identification

Following the release of the videos, the Philippine government launched a manhunt for the producers and the narrator.

### Arrest of Rodel Jayme
On April 30, 2019, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) arrested Rodel Jayme, the administrator of the website *metrobalita.net*, which had shared the videos . Jayme admitted to creating the website but denied uploading the videos or knowing the identity of "Bikoy." He claimed he was hired to set up the site for a fee . In May 2019, the DOJ indicted Jayme for inciting to sedition under the Cybercrime Prevention Act .

### Surfacing of Peter Joemel Advincula
On May 6, 2019, Peter Joemel Advincula appeared at the headquarters of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) in Pasig City. He identified himself as "Bikoy" and requested legal assistance to file cases against the individuals he named in the videos . At this time, Advincula stood by the content of the *Ang Totoong Narcolist* videos, claiming his life was in danger and that he wanted to clear his conscience . The IBP declined his request for legal aid .

## Retraction and "Project Sodoma"

On May 23, 2019, weeks after the midterm elections, Advincula surrendered to the PNP and was presented in a press conference. He completely recanted his previous statements, claiming the *Ang Totoong Narcolist* videos were fabricated .

Advincula alleged that the videos were part of "Project Sodoma," a plot orchestrated by the Liberal Party and Senator Antonio Trillanes IV to destabilize the government, oust President Duterte, and install Vice President Leni Robredo as President . He claimed the videos were scripted and that he was paid to act as the narrator . He implicated various opposition figures, including Senators Risa Hontiveros and Leila de Lima, as well as human rights lawyers and Catholic clergy, in the alleged conspiracy .

The opposition figures and lawyers named by Advincula categorically denied the allegations, calling them a "harassment suit" and questioning Advincula's credibility given his history of fraud convictions and shifting narratives .

## Related Events

### Oust Duterte Matrix
Shortly after the videos went viral, but before Advincula's retraction, Malacañang released an "Oust Duterte" matrix on April 22, 2019. The diagram linked various journalists, media organizations (such as Rappler and the Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism), and lawyers to an alleged plot to overthrow the President . The release of the matrix was criticized by the named groups as dangerous and baseless .

## Legal Proceedings

The controversy resulted in multiple legal battles involving the administration, the opposition, and Advincula himself.

### Sedition Complaint (2019)
Based on Advincula's sworn statement regarding "Project Sodoma," the PNP-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) filed a complaint in July 2019 against Vice President Robredo, Senator Trillanes, and over 30 others. The charges included sedition, inciting to sedition, cyber libel, and obstruction of justice .

### DOJ Resolution (2020)
In February 2020, the Department of Justice released its resolution regarding the PNP-CIDG complaint.
* **Cleared:** The DOJ dismissed the sedition charges against Vice President Leni Robredo, the Catholic bishops, and several other opposition figures due to lack of evidence .
* **Indicted:** The DOJ found probable cause to charge Antonio Trillanes IV, Peter Joemel Advincula, and nine others with "conspiracy to commit sedition" . The other indicted individuals included Joel Saracho, Boom Enriquez, Yolanda Ong, Vicente Romano III, Fr. Flaviano Villanueva, Fr. Albert Alejo, Jonnel Sangalang, and Eduardo Acierto .

### Perjury Conviction of Advincula (2023)
Lawyers from the Free Legal Assistance Group (FLAG)—Jose Manuel Diokno, Lorenzo Tañada III, and Theodore Te—filed a perjury case against Advincula. Advincula had claimed in his affidavit that he met with these lawyers at Ateneo de Manila University on March 4, 2019, to plan "Project Sodoma" .

On May 24, 2023, the Manila Metropolitan Trial Court Branch 17 found Advincula guilty beyond reasonable doubt of perjury. The court ruled that Advincula made a "willful and corrupt assertion of a falsehood," as evidence proved the lawyers were not present at the alleged meeting or that the meeting did not occur as described . Advincula was sentenced to an indeterminate penalty of three months and one day to one year and one day of imprisonment .

### Acquittal in Sedition Case (2023)
The conspiracy to commit sedition case against Trillanes, Advincula, and their co-accused was heard by the Quezon City Metropolitan Trial Court. On September 6, 2023, the court granted the demurrer to evidence filed by the defense, effectively acquitting all accused .

The court ruled that the prosecution failed to present sufficient evidence to prove the existence of a conspiracy. Crucially, the prosecution did not present Advincula as a witness to testify on the veracity of his sworn statement. The judge noted that without Advincula's testimony, his affidavit was hearsay and the "essential witness with personal knowledge of the entire incident was demonstrably not presented" .

20.content:
Police on Thursday filed a complaint of inciting to sedition against 38 people, including Vice President Maria Leonor “Leni” Robredo and other opposition figures, as well as eight Catholic clergymen, over the “Bikoy” video series uploaded on social media.

The complaint, by the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG), was based on the July 18 sworn affidavit of Peter Joemel Advincula, who accused opposition and church figures of using him to “spread lies against the President, his family and close associates.”

The Justice department said it had received the complaint and would form a panel of prosecutors to investigate.

Aside from inciting to sedition, the CIDG accused the 38, including Advincula, of cyber libel, libel, estafa, harboring a criminal and obstruction of justice.

Advincula, according to the CIDG complaint, claimed a plan was hatched at the Jesuit Communications office at Ateneo de Manila University in Quezon City, to topple President Rodrigo Duterte and install Robredo in Malacañang, as well as to improve the chances of the opposition slate in the May 2019 elections.

The 38 personalities were said to have conspired in producing and spreading the “Bikoy” or “_Ang Totoong Narcolist_” (The True Narcolist) videos on social media, with Advincula posing as the hooded and anonymous whistleblower “Bikoy.”

The videos linked Duterte and his family to illegal drugs.

Included in the complaint were senators Risa Hontiveros and Leila de Lima, as well as former senators Antonio Trillanes IV and Bam Aquino, and members of the opposition “Otso Diretso” slate, such as Jose Manuel Diokno and Lorenza Tañada III.

Also charged were Archbishop Socrates Villegas of Lingayen-Dagupan, Bishops Honesto Ongtioco of Cubao, Pablo Virgilio David of Caloocan and Teodoro Bacani, the former bishop of Novaliches, Fathers Flaviano Villanueva, Albert Alejo and Roberto Reyes, and Br. Armin Luistro, a former education secretary.

Advincula turned himself in to the police in May. He was said to have been under the protection of Catholic clergy.

The alleged conspiracy to bring down Duterte, which the Justice department said was dubbed “Project Sodoma,” supposedly began as early as August 2018. **_(PressONE.ph)_**

19.content:
PRESIDENTIAL daughter and Davao City Mayor Sara Duterte-Carpio on Thursday, May 24, 2019, dismissed Peter Joemel Advincula and called him a "scam" created by a disorganized anti-administration group.

"This group is so disorganized they cannot even get to first base because the path to their objective is in disarray," she said.

"Kung ako leader ng grupo na ito (If I were the leader of this group), I will shoot myself in the head, get rid of the brain that is not useful," she added.

The feisty mayor issued a comment at about the same time that Vice President Maria Leonor "Leni" Robredo and other Liberal Party (LP) leaders, Senator Antonio Trillanes IV and Otso Diretso candidates denied the fresh allegations made by Advincula.

Advincula, who maintained that he was the hooded man named "Bikoy" in the series of "Ang Totoong Narco-list" videos, surrendered Wednesday, May 22, 2019.

In a press conference Thursday, May 23, 2019, Advincula claimed that the videos were part of "Project Sodoma", a plot to oust President Rodrigo Duterte and install Robredo as new president.

He also said the videos were orchestrated by the Liberal Party and Trillanes.

Robredo and Trillanes have denied the allegations. Robredo said she does not know and has never met Advincula while Trillanes said Advincula's claims were just a ploy by the administration to harass the opposition.

Robredo also questioned the credibility of Advincula.

"Ako, sigurado ako na hindi siya credible, kasi noong sinabi niya ngang nag-meet kami sa Ateneo, never ko pa siyang na-meet sa aking buhay," she said.

Senator Francis Pangilinan, LP president, said Advincula's claims were fabricated by the administration to further discredit the opposition.

"Kahit ano sasabihin ng testigo laban sa mga nakaupo sa takot na masaktan. Wala kaming ugnayan sa video at kay Bikoy," Pangilinan said.

(He will say anything for fear that he will be harmed. We have nothing to do with the video and Bikoy.)

"Kasinungalingan lahat ang mga paratang na yan. Gawa-gawa lang ng administrasyon," he added.

(These accusations are all lies concocted by the administration.)

Senate Minority Leader and LP vice chairperson Franklin Drilon, for his part, urged the Philippine National Police to file charges against Advincula.

"The Liberal Party had nothing to do with the so-called Bikoy video. We deny the accusations that the Liberal Party connived with an obviously professional con artist to topple the government is most absurd. It is ridiculous on so many levels. It's excruciating to have listened to all his lies," he said.

"Having said that, I urge the Philippine National Police to get to the bottom of this Bikoy issue and file the appropriate charges," Drilon added.

Senator Panfilo Lacson, who is independent, said Advincula suffers from a "serious credibility problem." He said he was open to conduct an investigation into Advincula's claims if the man has solid evidence.

For now, he said he would leave it to the authorities to conduct the appropriate assessment on Advincula's revelations.

"As far as I am concerned, being a former law enforcement officer with quite good experience in intelligence and investigation, Bikoy has to show more than just a narration of what he says now as the real facts. He suffers from a serious credibility problem that he must overcome if he wants to be believed this time. He can only do it by presenting solid and substantial proof of his alleged meetings and regular communication with the people that he is now turning the tables on," he said.

Lacson earlier scheduled a Senate inquiry on the "Bikoy" videos following Advincula's appearance at the IBP but later cancelled the hearing, saying it was nonsense.

Magdalo party-list Representative Gary Alejano and Samira Gutoc, Otso Diretso candidates, said they have never met Advincula.

Alejano said he will sit down with fellow Otso Diretso candidates to decide on possible charges that will be filed against Advincula.

Gutoc said this amounts to political harassment by the administration.

Presidential son Paolo Duterte, meanwhile, called for the conduct of an investigation into Advincula's claims that Trillanes were behind all this.

"From the very start, it was clear that the Bikoy videos were fabricated with a narrative taken straight from the playbook of people whose desire is to destroy our name and our reputation," Paolo, the incoming Davao City Representative, said in a statement.

"All the lies presented were also meant to crush the trust of the Filipino people in the authorities and inspire public disgust against the government — truly the handiwork of people who want to undermine the Duterte administration," he added.

In the videos, the hooded man "Bikoy" claims that Paolo, Sara's husband Manases and senator-elect Christopher "Bong" Go have ties to an illegal drugs syndicate.

Advincula, who maintained the he is "Bikoy", said the allegations were all lies and apologized to the Duterte family.

He claimed that the video was orchestrated by the LP and Trillanes in a bid to make the administration's senatorial candidates lose the May 13, 2019 elections.

Nine of 12 senators elected in the recent elections were endorsed by Duterte. All Otso Diretso candidates, on the other hand, were defeated. **(SunStar Philippines)**

[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

On April 2, 2019, Peter Joemel Advincula, a former criminal, created a series of videos titled **"Ang Totoong Narcolist"** (transl. The True Narcolist). It discussed the alleged involvement of the [Duterte family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duterte_family "Duterte family") in drug syndicates, accusing politicians [Bong Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bong_Go "Bong Go") and [Paolo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte"), both closely related to the Duterte family. The videos garnered nationwide attention as politicians denied the accusations; a manhunt was also commenced.

During Advincula's childhood, he wanted to become a priest; he was introduced to a drug [syndicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syndicate "Syndicate"), which led to him being charged with [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud") in 2012. Advincula had to remain in prison for six years; he was released one year early in 2017 due to [good character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_conduct_time "Good conduct time"). After dwelling in prison, Advincula wanted to become a [whistleblower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whistleblowing "Whistleblowing"). He created a channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" in YouTube on April 2, 2019, based around a hooded whistleblower named "Bikoy". Five videos were produced, between April 2 and Advincula's surrender on May 6. The videos induced a manhunt for the perpetrator led by the [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_/(Philippines/) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)"). Originally, Rodel Jayme, the owner of a website which distributed the videos, was apprehended on April 30. Just before Jayme was convicted, Advincula surrendered to the police. He paid his bail and left [Camp Crame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Crame "Camp Crame"), where he was detained, yet returned to the police for protection. Numerous politicians were charged with sedition, including Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo") and Trillanes. The [Oust Duterte matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix "Oust Duterte matrix"), a diagram exhibiting participants of an alleged ouster plot, was released on April 22, soon after the controversy.

Advincula was born in 1989, in [Donsol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donsol "Donsol"), Sorsogon, Philippines. He was introduced to a drug syndicate operating in [Misibis Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misibis_Bay "Misibis Bay") on May 6, 2010, and was selected to head [closed-circuit television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed-circuit_television "Closed-circuit television") operations in underground facilities throughout the area. After, he was tasked to prepare the monthly "TARA", a document listing the collections and payoffs that month.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) During this time, Advincula allegedly witnessed the killing of one of his syndicate members, as well as the raping of the latter's wife and daughter.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlejo2020133-2)

[![Image 2: Refer to caption](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_/(cropped/).jpg)

A portrait of President Rodrigo Duterte

Advincula fled the syndicate due to a fear that he would be murdered. Eventually, [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_/(Philippines/) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)") (NBI) agents found Advincula. He attempted to run from them but was arrested, convicted of fraud in 2012, and sentenced to six years in prison. During the first three years, he was detained at the [Naga City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naga,_Camarines_Sur "Naga, Camarines Sur") District Jail. He was transferred to the [New Bilibid Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Bilibid_Prison "New Bilibid Prison") due to good behavior. In prison, he returned to his religious activities, serving as a "teacher" for the local detainees.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) Allegedly, during his detainment, he contacted the office of Senator [Tito Sotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tito_Sotto "Tito Sotto"). He attempted to expose the businessmen who connected him to the drug syndicate to leave the prison. Sotto did not reply, finding his claims "suspicious."[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:7-3) He was released in 2017, one year early due to good character.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1)

### Duterte administration

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Duterte administration")\]

Rodrigo Duterte won the [2016 Philippine presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Philippine_presidential_election "2016 Philippine presidential election") and assumed presidency on June 30.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-4) His presidency was controversial and marked by an intensive crackdown on [illegal drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_drugs "Illegal drugs"). In his [first 100 days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_100_days_of_Rodrigo_Duterte%27s_presidency "First 100 days of Rodrigo Duterte's presidency"), the [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) killed approximately 3,600 people under Duterte's command. This drew condemnation from the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), and other international organizations.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-5) Large protests have also been held against the administration of Duterte; many of them were against the PNP killings.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-6) In September 2018, an alleged ouster plot, titled [Red October](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_October_/(plot/) "Red October (plot)"), was allegedly found, reportedly created by members of the opposition.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-7) In March 2019, Duterte exposed 46 "narcolists," or politicians with connections to drug syndicates.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-8) Along with this, various disinformation campaigns were created leading up to the [2019 Philippine general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Philippine_general_election "2019 Philippine general election").[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-9) [Surigao del Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surigao_del_Norte "Surigao del Norte") Representative [Ace Barbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace_Barbers "Ace Barbers") portrayed these scandals as a possible motive for the creation of the "Bikoy" videos.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-10)

[![Image 3: A hooded figure staring in a black background](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/6/67/Bikoyvideostill.jpg/250px-Bikoyvideostill.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bikoyvideostill.jpg)

Still from _[The Philippine Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Philippine_Star "The Philippine Star")_ showing the hooded figure in an episode of the "Bikoy" series

In August 2018, Advincula planned to go into hiding and become a whistleblower; he wanted to expose the Misibis Bay syndicate's operations.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) He created a YouTube channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" (transl. The True Narcolist), set up on April 2, 2019. The videos are based around a hooded whistleblower named "Bikoy", who claimed to be a former member of drug syndicates in [Southern Luzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Luzon "Southern Luzon") and the [Visayas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visayas "Visayas") archipelago. According to _[Vera Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vera_Files "Vera Files")_, the videos seemed professionally done and had nice annotation.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11) Five videos were created in total, between April 2 and Advincula's surrender on May 6; the videos were widely circulated throughout social media.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12)

The first episode was released on April 2.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) It displayed papers that "Bikoy" claimed to be TARA documents related to the syndicate. According to "Bikoy", typical TARA documents contain a date, a code name and bank account of a high-ranking official, and deposits made. The bottom of the documents flaunted a signature which ensured that the details in the documents were accurate. "Bikoy" then presented two code names, saying that the code names were not "so bright" due to their similarity to criminals' real names. He claimed the first code name was associated with Waldo Carpio, the brother of [Sara Duterte's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte") husband, [Mans Carpio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mans_Carpio "Mans Carpio").[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-14) He then purported that the other code name belonged to [Paolo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte"), alleging that the latter had a tattoo on his back showing the code name.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:8-15)

The second episode was released five days later[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11) through [Bombo Radyo Iloilo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombo_Radyo_Iloilo "Bombo Radyo Iloilo"). It divulged a new code name, which according to "Bikoy", was difficult to trace. He eventually associated the names to three bank accounts, including one belonging to Elijah Manuel Pepito and another to Veronica Salvador. Pepito was the partner lawyer for Mans Carpio's law firm. "Veronica Salvador" was a merged name of Duterte's wife, [Honeylet "Salvador" Avanceña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a "Honeylet Avanceña"), and their daughter Kitty, shown as "Veronica".[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-16)

The third episode was released on April 8, the following day,[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-17) It discussed the alleged involvement of Senator [Bong Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bong_Go "Bong Go") in the drug trade. "Bikoy" claimed that drug money was being funneled to Go's account and insisted that Go had a dragon tattoo on his back with his code name.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:3-18) The fourth episode was released on April 12, four days later.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) In the video, "Bikoy" further argued that Go had a dragon tattoo and stated that he was confident of his allegation; he showed a picture of Go playing basketball with a portion of the dragon tattoo visible. In the video, he reiterated that Carpio was involved in drug operations.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-19) The fifth and final video was released on April 22. In it, "Bikoy" revealed alleged organizations related to the Misibis Bay syndicate and identified personalities he claimed were involved. He also exhibited the "Quadrangle Group", an alleged group of rich businessmen allegedly involved in drug operations.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13)

Numerous Duterte-aligned politicians opposed the videos. During the episodes' release, [Presidential Spokesperson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_spokesperson_/(Philippines/) "Presidential spokesperson (Philippines)") [Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo") said that the allegations mentioned were "[black propaganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_propaganda "Black propaganda")" and that "Bikoy" was just a "pawn." He also accused the [Liberal Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_/(Philippines/) "Liberal Party (Philippines)") of creating the videos.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-20) After the first video, President Duterte blamed the political opposition and hinted that Senator [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") was likely behind it, calling him [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay").[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-21) Due to Advincula's allegations that Bong Go has a dragon tattoo, Go has shown his back on two occasions: at a [Hugpong ng Pagbabago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugpong_ng_Pagbabago "Hugpong ng Pagbabago") campaign event[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:3-18) and later at a [Luntiang Pilipinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luntiang_Pilipinas "Luntiang Pilipinas") campaign event in [Calamba, Laguna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calamba,_Laguna "Calamba, Laguna").[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-22) Trillanes praised the videos, wishing to have been part of the videos' creation. He then challenged [Paolo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte") to display the tattoo on his back, which Duterte refused to do.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:8-15) The Liberal Party denied their involvement[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-23) while [Communist Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Philippines "Communist Party of the Philippines") founder [Jose Maria Sison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Maria_Sison "Jose Maria Sison") said "Bikoy" should be given protection to tell his story.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-24) The [Department of Justice of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Justice_/(Philippines/) "Department of Justice (Philippines)") (DOJ) questioned "Bikoy"'s credibility due to his anonymity.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-25) The videos were considered a controversial topic online: viewers shared documents from the video, with a [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") page titled "for the motherland Sass Rogando Sasot" encountering connections between the documents shown to a bank in [Legazpi, Albay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legazpi,_Albay "Legazpi, Albay").[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-26) According to the [Philippine News Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_News_Agency "Philippine News Agency"), the videos were "publicly viewed, shared and uploaded" multiple times.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12)

### Oust Duterte matrix

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Oust Duterte matrix")\]

Shortly after the release of the videos, specifically on April 16, Duterte reported in a speech that he had received intelligence reports detailing an alleged ouster plot. Six days later, Panelo released the "Oust Duterte matrix," on the president's orders. The matrix named journalists from several news outlets, particularly the [Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Center_for_Investigative_Journalism "Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism") and _[Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler")_. Panelo said those journalists could be feeding their stories to "enemies of the state," or the opposition. He stated that the matrix was released to expose those behind the alleged ouster plot and did not file charges against the journalists shown in the matrix.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-27)

Manhunt and investigation
-------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Manhunt and investigation")\]

### Rodel Jayme's arrest

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Rodel Jayme's arrest")\]

The DOJ began investigating the videos April 17.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:5-28) The cybercrime division of the [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_/(Philippines/) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)") (NBI) said that the website "metrobalita.net", a page which shared the videos, was owned by blogger Rodel Jayme. He was arrested in his residence in [Parañaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para%C3%B1aque "Parañaque") April 30 and detained in NBI headquarters.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:4-29) Jayme was them charged with [sedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedition "Sedition") on May 2, with DOJ Secretary [Menardo Guevarra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menardo_Guevarra "Menardo Guevarra") saying he could also be charged with child abuse for mentioning Duterte's daughter in one of the videos.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:5-28) Jayme accused opposition groups of forcing him to create the websites. An NBI spokesperson said that Jayme could be a state witness for the accusations.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-30)

### Peter Advincula's arrest

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Peter Advincula's arrest")\]

Just before Jayme was to be charged, Peter Advincula, the original "Bikoy", emerged. He requested help from the [Integrated Bar of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_Bar_of_the_Philippines "Integrated Bar of the Philippines") (IBP) in suing the Dutertes and their allies,[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-31) maintaining his allegations were true. Two days later, the IBP rejected his offer. He then asked Senator [Panfilo Lacson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panfilo_Lacson "Panfilo Lacson") to postpone his hearing until the elections.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-32) That same day, Guevarra gave Advincula an ultimatum: bring evidence to back up his claims in the videos to the NBI, or face sedition charges.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-33) Advincula surrendered to police May 22, stating on national television that he played a role in a script made by the Liberal Party.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-34)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-35)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlejo2020132-36) The media called this reversal "[flip-flopping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip-flop_/(politics/) "Flip-flop (politics)")".[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:7-3) He also accused Trillanes of taking part in the video's production.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-37) The DOJ said that his allegations would need a deep investigation.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-38) [Solicitor General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solicitor_General_of_the_Philippines "Solicitor General of the Philippines") [Jose Calida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Calida "Jose Calida") offered legal aid to Advincula.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-39) Advincula had his [mugshot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mug_shot "Mug shot") on May 23.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-40) [Elizaldy Co](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizaldy_Co "Elizaldy Co"), one of the people mentioned in the videos, filed a 1 billion PHP lawsuit for damage from the accusations relating to him.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-41)

The next day, Advincula, charged with for six counts of [estafa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud"), paid 6,000 [PHP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_peso "Philippine peso") in bail.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-42) The next day, he left Camp Crame, where he was detained.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-43) The [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) started an investigation against Advincula[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-44) yet skipped a case hearing on the investigation the following day.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-45) He turned himself in to the police for protection on June 3, claiming that his life was in danger.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-46) The next day, the DOJ concluded their investigation, charging him with fraud, without a statement from Advincula.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-47) Trillanes released texts from Advincula for the production of the videos.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-48) Advincula was released from protective custody on June 25.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-49) [Ako Bicol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ako_Bicol "Ako Bicol") Representative [Alfredo Garbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfredo_Garbin "Alfredo Garbin") filed a resolution on May 29 for the [Philippine House Committee on Information and Communications Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_House_Committee_on_Information_and_Communications_Technology "Philippine House Committee on Information and Communications Technology") to investigate the potential effects of misinformation on social media platforms due to the videos.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12) The resolution resulted in investigations against Facebook and Google and a request for both to attend the hearing.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-50)

Numerous politicians were sued for sedition on July 18, including Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo").[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-51) Investigations began into his and other politicians' connection to the "Bikoy" videos.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-52) Advincula surrendered again to the PNP July 29.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-53)[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-54) He posted 10,000 PHP bail two days later[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-55) and then applied for state protection on August 5 with his lawyer [Larry Gadon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Gadon "Larry Gadon").[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-56) Two Catholic bishops were also charged with sedition later that month due to an alleged conversation with Advincula.[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-57) On August 20, Calida linked the videos to servers in the [Ateneo de Manila University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ateneo_de_Manila_University "Ateneo de Manila University").[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-58) Robredo responded to the investigations with a counter-affidavit, denying the accusations on August 29.[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-59) In September, a former lawyer of Trillanes stated that the senator had ties to "Bikoy"; the senator denied the accusation.[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-60) On February 10, 2020, Robredo was cleared of the charges against her, while [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") and actor [Joel Saracho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Saracho "Joel Saracho"), among others, were charged with sedition.[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-61)

Aftermath and legacy
--------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Aftermath and legacy")\]

On January 20, 2021, Advincula was charged with [perjury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perjury "Perjury") by a Manila court for allegedly false statements against the [Free Legal Assistance Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Legal_Assistance_Group "Free Legal Assistance Group").[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-62)[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-63) A warrant was issued for his arrest.[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-64) He surrendered at a local police station in [Daraga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daraga "Daraga"), posting 18,000 PHP bail.[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-65) He was absent from the court on July 21, causing the court to reissue his arrest warrant due to Advincula being unable to justify his absence.[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-66) Advincula allegedly killed three politicians in [Albay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albay "Albay") on November 13, with their bodies appearing in his [ukay-ukay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukay-ukay "Ukay-ukay") store in Daraga. He was declared the primary suspect.[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-67)[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-68) According to local police, his possible motive was a grudge between him and one of the victims after the man rejected Advincula's request for a loan.[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-69) He posted the 1 million PHP bail on December 16.[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-70) Two years later, he was convicted of perjury in statements he made in 2019 implicating lawyers [Erin Tañada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erin_Ta%C3%B1ada "Erin Tañada"), [Chel Diokno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chel_Diokno "Chel Diokno"), and [Theodore Te](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Te "Theodore Te") in an ouster plot.[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-71)[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-72) He was sentenced to a maximum of one year and one day in prison.[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-73) but eventually posted bail soon after the verdict.[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-74) In 2020, a journal released by the [Ateneo de Manila University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ateneo_de_Manila_University "Ateneo de Manila University") detailed the videos.[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlejo2020126-75) On October 8, 2024, Advincula filed his candidacy for senator in the [2025 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Philippine_Senate_election "2025 Philippine Senate election"), pushing for a centralized correctional system in the Philippines[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-76)[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-77) but he was declared a [nuisance candidate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuisance_candidate "Nuisance candidate") by the [Commission on Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Elections_/(Philippines/) "Commission on Elections (Philippines)").[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-78)

Accusing videos went viral during 2019 poll season

‘Bikoy’ gets 1 year for perjury; ‘vindication’ for opposition
=============================================================

By: [Abby Boiser](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/byline/abby-boiser), [Jacob Lazaro](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/byline/jacob-lazaro) - [@inquirerdotnet](https://www.twitter.com/@inquirerdotnet)

[Philippine Daily Inquirer](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/source/philippine-daily-inquirer) / 05:38 AM May 25, 2023

Share:

![Image 32: Peter Joemel Advincula STORY: ‘Bikoy’ gets 1 year for perjury; ‘vindication’ for opposition](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/files/2023/05/476473-620x437.jpeg)Peter Joemel Advincula (INQUIRER FILE PHOTO)

MANILA, Philippines — Peter Joemel Advincula, the video blogger known as “Bikoy” who in 2019 first accused the Duterte family of amassing drug money only to do an about-face by claiming his allegations were part of an opposition takeover plot, was sentenced to a maximum prison term of one year for perjury or lying to the court.

Advincula, who admitted to being the hooded figure in the viral “Ang Totoong Narco-list” videos, was meted an indeterminate penalty of at least three months and one day to a maximum of one year and one day in prison.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

In her 16-page decision, Judge Karla Funtila-Abugan of the Manila Metropolitan Trial Court Branch 17 said the actions of the accused met the “essential elements” of perjury, defined under Article 183 of the Revised Penal Code as “the willful and corrupt assertion of a falsehood under oath or affirmation administered by authority of law on a material matter.”

Advincula is out on bail and has the option of appealing the decision.

In an earlier affidavit, Advincula described the case as a “nuisance or harassment suit” aimed at obstructing sedition charges against the opposition figures he had accused of plotting to overthrow the government. The sedition charges were dismissed in 2020.

‘It’s a vindication’
--------------------

“To us it’s a vindication and now the truth has been exposed to everyone that we really had nothing to do with that,” said law school dean Chel Diokno, a member of the Otso Diretso senatorial ticket accused by Advincula of trying to unseat then President Rodrigo Duterte.

“The accusations were quite serious that we were allegedly involved in seditious acts, and that we wanted to manipulate the results of the election, which all turned out to be false and fake,” Diokno told the Inquirer on Wednesday.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

“That is why for us, this is a vindication,” he said.

Diokno and the rest of the Otso Diretso team, including former Quezon Rep. Erin Tañada, lost the elections to administration candidates.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

In April 2019, videos showing a hooded man who linked members of Duterte’s family to the illegal drug trade were posted on Facebook.

The man, who only called himself Bikoy, claimed Duterte’s son Paolo, son-in-law Manases Carpio and former aide Christopher Go, now a senator, were members of an illegal drug syndicate who had collected millions of pesos in drug money.

On May 6, 2019, days before the May 13 elections, Advincula surfaced at the Integrated Bar of the Philippines main office in Pasig City, claiming to be the Bikoy in the videos.

He told reporters that he had wanted to show that the President’s family and associates benefited from the narcotics trade. He also sought legal aid in filing cases.

‘Project Sodoma’
----------------

But on May 23, 2019, after the opposition shutout in the elections, Advincula said his previous claims were false and that the videos had been part of a scheme to unseat Duterte hatched by the Liberal Party and Sen. Antonio Trillanes IV.

Advincula, who had admitted to being jailed for fraud, also linked Sen. Risa Hontiveros and a staff member of then Sen. Leila de Lima to the so-called “Project Sodoma,” which he said was intended to topple Duterte from power and install then Vice President Leni Robredo, who was to pick Trillanes as her vice president.

In July 2019, Robredo and 31 other opposition figures were charged with sedition and other offenses based solely on the claims of Advincula, who by then had turned into a government witness.

On Sept. 6, 2019, lawyers implicated in the sedition raps, Diokno, Tañada and lawyer Theodore Te, filed a countersuit against Advincula and Police Lt. Col. Arnold Thomas Ibay of the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group, saying they made false statements in making the accusations against them.

In February 2020, the Department of Justice cleared Robredo and several opposition figures, Catholic prelates and lawyers of sedition charges.

Murder charges
--------------

Advincula, on the other hand, is still facing multiple murder charges in the killing of three local election candidates from Sorsogon City who were found dead in Advincula’s thrift store in Daraga town, Albay, in 2021.

While Advincula’s conviction on the perjury charge was good news for the opposition, Diokno admitted that the damage to his and his colleagues’ reputations had already been done.

“I would find it highly questionable to believe that he could have done this all by himself,” the rights lawyer said, adding: “Who made Advincula do what he did — that’s a big question that should be looked into.”

“The truth about that will also come out as the days pass, there’s no ‘forever’ in lying,” Diokno said.

WHAT WENT BEFORE: ‘True Narcolist’ video
========================================

07:24 AM May 07, 2019

Share:

[![Image 24: Copy Link](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/copy-link.svg)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1114686/what-went-before-true-narcolist-video#)

[![Image 26: Bookmark](blob:https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/76f70cba1a4985ff842bd808acca549c)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1114686/what-went-before-true-narcolist-video#)

[![Image 28: Facebook](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/fb-share.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsinfo.inquirer.net%2F1114686%2Fwhat-went-before-true-narcolist-video)

[![Image 30: X](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/x-share.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsinfo.inquirer.net%2F1114686%2Fwhat-went-before-true-narcolist-video)

MANILA, Philippines — On April 2, a six-minute video titled “Ang Totoong Narcolist (True Narcolist) Episode 1” was posted on Facebook, showing a hooded man who claimed President Duterte’s son Paolo Duterte received payoffs from a drug syndicate.

The man identified himself as Bikoy and he said Paolo Duterte was known in the syndicate by the code name Alpha Tierra-0029.

Bikoy also showed a list containing the names of alleged drug lords and the money they had in their bank accounts.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

The first video was followed by others where Bikoy accused other people close to President Duterte, including his 15-year-old daughter Veronica, former special presidential assistant Christopher “Bong” Go, and lawyer Manases Carpio, husband of Davao City Mayor Sara Duterte, of accepting payoffs from the syndicate.

FEATURED STORIES

NEWSINFO

[Magalong: Cabral’s last stop a probed project site](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2157658/magalong-cabrals-last-stop-a-probed-project-site)

NEWSINFO

[Evidence shows 'suicide' in Cabral’s death – PNP](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2157778/evidence-shows-suicide-in-cabrals-death-pnp)

NEWSINFO

[Plunder, graft cases filed vs Recto, Ledesma over PhilHealth fund transfer](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2157834/plunder-graft-cases-filed-vs-recto-ledesma-over-philhealth-fund-transfer)

Bikoy said other politicians and some businessmen from Bicol region had links to the illegal drug trade.

He said he had documents from the time he started working for the drug syndicate in 2010.

Bikoy said he handled the financial records of the ring, which operated in Southern Luzon and in the Visayas.

He said the code name Polo Delta was actually Paolo Duterte, who allegedly had bank accounts held for him by Agriculture Undersecretary Waldo Carpio, brother of Manases Carpio.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

In the syndicate’s financial transactions, he said, Paolo Duterte was referred to as Polo Delta-TSG01.

Bikoy said he left the syndicate last year.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

He said he decided to disclose what he knew about Paolo Duterte’s involvement in the illegal drug trade after President Duterte released his list of so-called narcopoliticians.

“I left the syndicate and tried to lead a new life. But the syndicate did not leave me alone and I’m now getting death threats,” Bikoy said. —_Inquirer Research_

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has dropped six criminal charges against former Sen. Antonio “Sonny” Trillanes IV but pursued the case of conspiracy to commit sedition with 10 other persons in connection with the publication of “Ang Totoong Narcolist” video blogs by a certain “Bikoy” in early 2019.

A three-man DoJ panel submitted to the Quezon City Metropolitan Trial Court on Feb. 10 a 57-page resolution dated Jan. 27 to indict Trillanes along with Peter Joemel Advincula, Joel Saracho, Yolanda Villanueva Ong, Boom Enriquez, Jonnel Sangalang, Eduardo Acierto, Vicente Romano III, Catholic priests Flaviano Villanueva and Albert Alejo, and an alias “Monique.”

In a Feb. 10 statement, DOJ Spokesperson Markk Perete said the prosecution panel found probable cause to charge with conspiracy to commit sedition the 11 out of 30 respondents in the criminal complaint filed by the Philippine National Police-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (PNP-CIDG) in July 2019.

Conspiracy to commit sedition is punishable under Article 141 of the Revised Penal Code with imprisonment of two years, four months and one day to four years and two months, and a fine of up to P2,000.

Trillanes, in a statement, immediately dismissed his indictment as an “absurd case” and considered it as yet “another proof that the Duterte administration continues to weaponize the law against the political opposition, critics and the media.”

“But let me assure Mr. Duterte that we will not be cowed by such political persecution. On the contrary, we are more determined and motivated to continue our fight for democracy and the rights of our people,” the former senator vowed.

While pursuing the conspiracy to commit sedition case against Trillanes et al, the DOJ prosecutors dismissed the cases of sedition, inciting to sedition, cyber libel, libel, estafa, and obstruction of justice lodged by the PNP-CIDG against all 30 respondents that included Vice President Leni Robredo and outspoken Caloocan Bishop Pablo David.

Perete said that while the “Ang Totoong Narcolist” video series may have “libelous imputations” against Duterte, it did not find words that “tended to incite the people to take up arms or rise against the government.”

“In finding no probable cause for sedition or inciting to sedition, the panel found the element of public and tumultuous uprising wanting,” he explained.

But then, he said: “The panel explained that \[there\] were ‘interlocking pieces of proof’ \[that\] provide ‘a complete picture of the grand conspiracy between and among some respondents to create hatred or revenge against the President and his family with the end view of toppling and destabilizing the current administration.’”

The prosecutors cited four circumstances to prove the alleged conspiracy to discredit and eventually topple the Duterte administration. These were:

*   The publication on the internet of “Ang Totoong Narcolist” video series that featured alias Bikoy spewing accusations that Duterte, his family, and former aide-turned-senator Christopher Lawrence “Bong” Go were among those receiving money from illegal drug trade. The panel said Saracho, Enriquez, “Monique”, Ong and Romano III were involved in the filming and production of the videos. It added that Alejo prepared “JesCom”, referring to Jesuit Communications, as the venue for the videos shoot.
*   The May 7, 2019 press conference of Advincula at the Integrated Bar of the Philippines headquarters where he “admitted” to being Bikoy.
*   The March 25, 2019 press statement of Acierto linking “Duterte, his family, and political allies” to drugs and drug syndicates.
*   The admissions of respondents, including Trillanes, that prove the “existence of a grand conspiracy” to commit sedition.

Advincula, who has made contradicting statements before and after surrendering to the police, claimed that several members of the opposition and Catholic priests and bishops were involved in “Project Sodoma,” which sought to oust Duterte and to place Robredo and Trillanes as president and vice-president, respectively, and to boost the candidacy in the 2019 senatorial elections of the Otso Diretso candidates of the Liberal Party.

To date, Trillanes, a staunch critic of Duterte, is facing at least three sedition-related complaints all filed under the Duterte administration.

Responding to the dropping of the charges against Robredo, her spokesperson Ibarra “Barry” Gutierrez said in a statement that it was “a clear condemnation” of the trumped up charges against the vice president and the other accused.

“Ang resolusyon ng Department of Justice Special Panel of Prosecutors na nagsasabing walang ebidensiya laban kay Bise Presidente Leni Robredo at nananawagang ibasura ang criminal complaint laban sa kaniya at 25 (sic) pang iba ay malinaw na pagkondena sa mga gawa-gawang akusasyon na pilit ibinabato sa kaniya,” Gutierrez said.

[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The **Oust Duterte** matrix was a diagram released on April 22, 2019, after the [Ang Totoong Narcolist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist "Ang Totoong Narcolist") YouTube channel controversy, where the channel speculated about the involvement of Duterte in drug syndicates. The diagram, released by the [Office of the President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaca%C3%B1ang_Palace "Malacañang Palace"), claimed to reveal links between journalists and organizations with plans to oust President [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-:2-1) It was officially released by Presidential Spokesperson [Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo"), who said that it underwent "proper validation." The matrix named journalists from multiple news websites, including the [_Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Center_for_Investigative_Journalism "Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism") and _[Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler")_. Another version was released on May 8 along with a [Microsoft PowerPoint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_PowerPoint "Microsoft PowerPoint") presentation. People who were included in the matrix denied they had plans to oust Duterte. Following the release of the matrix, one of the groups sought government protection from harassment, while a newspaper editor resigned.

In an interview with [Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler") in late 2015, Duterte announced his candidacy for president in the 2016 Philippine presidential election.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-2) He filed his Certificate of Candidacy (COC) for the elections a few days later, withdrawing from the mayoral race of [Davao City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davao_City "Davao City").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-3) After intense competition, he won with more than 16.6 million votes.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-4) His presidency was controversial, marked by an intensive crackdown on [illegal drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_drugs "Illegal drugs"). In his [first 100 days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_100_days_of_Rodrigo_Duterte%27s_presidency "First 100 days of Rodrigo Duterte's presidency"), the [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) killed approximately 3,600 people, with thousands of raids conducted. Because of this, he was criticized by the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), and other organizations.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-5) An [ouster plot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_October_/(ouster_plot/) "Red October (ouster plot)") was announced by Duterte on September 8, 2018. It was allegedly planned by the [Communist Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Philippines "Communist Party of the Philippines"),[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-6) which had previously assisted Duterte in the formation of his cabinet in 2016.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-8) After the announcement, the alleged plot "fell apart," according to politician [Delfin Lorenzana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delfin_Lorenzana "Delfin Lorenzana").[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-:0-9) A YouTube channel, named "[Ang Totoong Narcolist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist "Ang Totoong Narcolist")", was created in April 2019, alleging the involvement of Duterte in drug syndicates.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-:1-10) Because of the videos, the alleged perpetrator and Senator [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") were charged with [sedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedition "Sedition"), with the latter cleared of charges a year later.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-11)

Release and aftermath
---------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oust_Duterte_matrix&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Release and aftermath")\]

[![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/9f/OustDuterteMatrix.jpg/250px-OustDuterteMatrix.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:OustDuterteMatrix.jpg)

Presidential Spokesperson [Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo") holding a copy of the matrix

After the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" YouTube channel caused controversy, a matrix was announced by presidential spokesperson [Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo") on April 22. [Malacañang Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaca%C3%B1ang_Palace "Malacañang Palace"), the office of the President of the Philippines, was scheduled to publish the diagram officially, but [_The Manila Times_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Manila_Times "The Manila Times") beat them to it, prompting Panelo to question how the newspaper obtained it early.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-:2-1) The matrix contained the names of journalists and organizations who allegedly want to oust Duterte, with journalists from the _Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism_ (PCIJ) and _Rappler_. Panelo said that there was a "basis to release it" and that the matrix underwent "proper validation," stating that "the President has so many sources, so he got the matrix from one of his sources." He also shared the possibility of the journalists "feeding their stories to the enemies of the state."[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-:2-1) Another version of the matrix was released on May 8, with a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation to support the claims. The other version included "active online collaboration" between former presidential spokesperson [Edwin Lacierda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Lacierda "Edwin Lacierda") and other people, journalist Ellen Tordesillas being part of "controversy" along with the [Liberal Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_/(Philippines/) "Liberal Party (Philippines)") and the [Magdalo Party-List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magdalo_Party-List "Magdalo Party-List"), and other alleged links.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-12)

Filipino Olympian [Hidilyn Diaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidilyn_Diaz "Hidilyn Diaz") was "shocked" over her inclusion in the matrix. In a post shared on May 8, Diaz joked about her inclusion.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-13) [Maria Ressa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Ressa "Maria Ressa"), the CEO of _Rappler_, who was included in the matrix, said that it was "garbage" and a "Palace ploy to harass journalists." Ellen Tordesillas, an editor of [_Vera Files_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vera_Files "Vera Files"), which was also included in the matrix, denied the allegations, stating that it was "downright false." The PCIJ said the report was "wrong on many points," saying that they have never received an email from Tordesillas about the YouTube channel. The rest of Rappler said that the report was an example of "how not to write an investigative report or even straight news."[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-14) A former member of the National Union of Peoples' Lawyers, [Inday Espina-Varona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inday_Espina-Varona "Inday Espina-Varona"), and a former member of Vera Files, Luz Rumban, both said that they left their respective companies, with Rumban leaving in 2018.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-15) Magdalo Party-List Representative and opposition member [Gary Alejano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Alejano "Gary Alejano") branded the matrix as "utterly irresponsible" in a press briefing on April 22, demanding Panelo and Duterte resign over it.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-16) Numerous groups labeled the matrix as "ludicrous" and "dangerous".[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-17) Netizens mocked the creation of the matrix, stating that it lacked information. Some netizens made their own versions of the matrix with [Marvel heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Heroes_And_villains "Marvel Heroes And villains") and [cockroaches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cockroach "Cockroach").[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-18)

Members of the National Union of Peoples' Lawyers were harassed for their security and safety. Through the union, they submitted an eight-page manifestation detailing this harassment to the [Supreme Court of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_Philippines "Supreme Court of the Philippines") and asked for government protection.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-19) An editor for The Manila Times resigned on April 26 because the first article was "poorly sourced." In an interview, the editor was allegedly asked to resign from the newspaper. He said that it could have been written in a journalistic manner but appeared to be "an opinion piece".[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-20) According to opposition members, the matrix attempted to distract citizens from the upcoming [2019 Philippine general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Philippine_general_election "2019 Philippine general election") and allegedly attempted to "cripple the nation's democracy".[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-21) According to multiple groups, the matrix proved that the Duterte administration purposely shamed administration critics by alleging them to be government destabilizers.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlemm_et_al.202365-22)

DOJ indicts Trillanes, ‘Bikoy’ and 9 others of conspiracy to commit sedition
============================================================================

By: [Tetch Torres-Tupas](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/byline/tetch-torres-tupas) - Reporter / [@T2TupasINQ](https://www.twitter.com/@T2TupasINQ)

Share:

[![Image 30: X](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/x-share.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsinfo.inquirer.net%2F1226755%2Fdoj-indicts-trillanes-bikoy-and-9-others-of-conspiracy-to-commit-sedition)

MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed a criminal case against former senator Antonio Trillanes IV and 10 others for their involvement in the “Ang Totoong Narcolist” videos that linked President Rodrigo Duterte, his family to the illegal drug trade.

Aside from Trillanes, also charged before the Metropolitan Trial Court in Quezon City were the following:

\-Peter Joemel Advincula, the man who introduced himself as “Bikoy” in the “Ang Totoong Narcolist” videos released during the 2019 election campaign period

In its 57-page resolution dated Jan. 27, 2020, the details of which were made public Monday, said there was enough evidence to indict the 11 respondents of conspiracy to commit sedition.

Citing Article 141 of the Revised Penal Code, the Panel noted that criminal liability arises for individuals who conspire or agree to raise commotions and disturbances to attain by force, intimidation, or any other means outside of the legal methods any of the following objectives: a) to prevent the promulgation or execution of any law or the holding of any popular election;  b) to prevent the National Government, or any Provincial or Municipal Government, or any public officer thereof, from freely exercising its or his functions, or prevent the execution of any administrative order; c) to inflict any act of hate or revenge upon the person or property of any public officer or employee; d) to commit, for any political or social end, any act of hate or revenge against private persons or any social class; and e) to despoil, for any political or social end, any person, municipality or province, or the National Government of all its property or any part thereof.

Rodel Jayme pleads not guilty to inciting to sedition
=====================================================

By NICOLE-ANNE C. LAGRIMAS, GMA News

**Published** May 21, 2019 3:14pm  

Rodel Jayme, the man arrested for allegedly sharing anti-Duterte videos on his website, on Tuesday pleaded not guilty to a charge of inciting to sedition.

Jayme entered the plea at his arraignment at the Parañaque Regional Trial Court Branch 258, where the Department of Justice had charged him with inciting to sedition in relation to the anti-cybercrime law, an offense punishable by a prison term of six to 12 years.

The 27-year-old Jayme admitted creating the metrobalita.net website, which the DOJ said was among the first to share a series of YouTube videos that implicated members of the First Family in the illegal drug trade. He, however, denied uploading the videos.

Justifying its charge, the DOJ said the posting of the videos is not an exercise of Jayme's freedom of speech and expression but a "clear act to arouse among its viewers a sense of dissatisfaction against the duly constituted authorities."

The court also ordered Jayme transferred to the Parañaque City Jail from the National Bureau of Investigation.

Jayme earlier expressed willingness to identify the persons behind the scheme. The NBI had said it may consider moving for the webmaster's discharge as a state witness.

Meanwhile, Peter Joemel Advincula, the man who claims to be the First Family's accuser "Bikoy" in the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" videos, has yet to face charges in connection with the allegations.

An admitted estafa convict supposedly released from prison in 2016, Advincula faces a new estafa complaint at the DOJ. **—KBK, GMA News**

32.content:
Paolo Duterte resigned as vice mayor of Davao City in December 2017, months after he was implicated in the smuggling of P6.4 billion worth of illegal drugs. He refused to undergo a drug test or bare his back, which supposedly had a dragon-like tattoo signifying his membership in a triad.

Fast forward to 2024; Duterte, the incumbent representative of Davao City in Congress and son of former president Rodrigo Duterte, files a bill seeking to require random drug tests on all elected and appointed government officials, including the president, every six months.

The timing of the bill is suspect, of course. The Dutertes have come up with several exposés, albeit of dubious origin, to pin down President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on their repeated allegation that he has used or is using cocaine.

Between 2017 and 2024, the tides turned on the Dutertes, who were all-powerful when Rodrigo was president and daughter Sara was mayor of Davao City. Although Sara is still the country’s vice president, she has been sidelined for more than a year following her election as Marcos’ running mate under the 2022 UniTeam alliance and deprived of more than half a billion pesos in confidential funds.

News reports say Paolo Duterte’s bill was filed last Aug. 12, four days before the so-called quad committee in the House of Representatives had its first public hearing in Bacolor, Pampanga.

In that hearing, Jimmy Guban, a former customs intelligence officer serving a life sentence for drug smuggling, implicated Paolo, his brother-in-law Manases Carpio and his father’s former economic adviser Michael Yang in an P11-billion drug shipment in 2018.

Guban said Paolo Duterte and Carpio, the husband of Vice President Sara Duterte, were part of a conspiracy to smuggle 355 kilograms of “shabu” (crystal meth) hidden in steel magnetic lifters that passed inspection by the Bureau of Customs after they arrived at the Manila International Container Terminal in August 2018.

The House leadership has authorized the “quadcom” to conduct a comprehensive joint investigation into a possible connection between illegal Philippine offshore gambling operators, illegal drugs, extrajudicial killings and human rights violations in the course of the former president’s bloody drug war.

The “quadcom” is composed of the Committees on Dangerous Drugs, chaired by Surigao del Norte Rep. Robert Ace Barbers; Public Order and Safety, chaired by Laguna Rep. Dan Fernandez; Human Rights, chaired by Manila Rep. Bienvenido Abante Jr.; and Public Accounts, chaired by Abang Lingkod Party-list Rep. Joseph Stephen Paduano.

In the P6.4 billion worth of drugs shipped from China in May 2017, which the Senate investigated that same year, Paolo Duterte and Carpio were also implicated but were later cleared by the committee chaired by then-senator Richard Gordon for lack of sufficient evidence.

The Office of the Ombudsman also cleared Duterte and Carpio in May 2018, saying, “The complaints against former Davao City vice mayor Paolo Duterte … were dismissed for lack of basis.”

Paolo Duterte and Carpio faced a Senate investigation in September 2017 on the allegation of then-senator Antonio Trillanes IV that they were connected to a Chinese drug cartel known as the Davao Group that was responsible for the shipment of more than 600 kilograms of shabu seized at a port in Manila.

Trillanes claimed that Paolo Duterte had a dragon-like tattoo on his back that is known to be worn by Chinese triad members. Duterte admitted having a tattoo on his back but refused to describe or show it, invoking his right to privacy.

In April 2019, a two-part video titled “_Ang Totoong Narcolist_” was uploaded on YouTube and the Facebook account of “Metro Balita,” which claims to be a “media/news company.” The video showed a hooded whistleblower, who identified himself as “Bikoy” and claimed to be a former member of a drug syndicate operating in Southern Luzon and the Visayas region.

Alias “Bikoy” claimed that Paolo Duterte and Carpio were part of a drug syndicate. The video was released just two weeks after the former president came out with an initial list of local officials allegedly involved in drug trafficking.

After he was cleared by the Senate and the Ombudsman of involvement in a 2017 drug smuggling case, Paolo Duterte’s name cropped up again in a revived probe on a bigger drug haul in 2018.

A witness in the 2017 probe, Customs broker Mark Taguba retracted his testimony and apologized to Duterte and Carpio for having dragged their names into the P6.4-billion shabu shipment.

Guban, who was detained for seven weeks in the Senate in 2018 after he was cited in contempt for inconsistent statements, is now singing a different tune.

Can the House “quadcom” succeed in ferreting out the truth in those big drug hauls and hold accountable those behind the illegal drug trading in the country? Does Paulo Duterte still have a dragon-like tattoo on his back and will he be willing to bare his back to prove his accusers wrong?
